172	### ISC Quality System
173	
174	**Every criterion describes one verifiable end-state.** The operational test is granularity:
175	
176	> **Split until each criterion is one binary tool probe.** A criterion is granular enough when a single tool call (`Read`, `Grep`, `Bash`, `curl`, screenshot, `SELECT`, `bun test`, etc.) returns yes/no on whether it's met. If you cannot name the probe, the criterion is not yet atomic — split it. If the criterion needs human judgment, name the tool-verifiable proxy that stands in for the judgment.
177	
178	**Tier floor:** the granularity rule produces a natural N. At E2+, that N must meet the tier ISC floor (E2 ≥16, E3 ≥32, E4 ≥128, E5 ≥256). For complex-app project ISAs, the ISC count naturally runs much higher. E1 has no floor — fast-path stays fast.
179	
180	**Splitting Test** — apply to every criterion as you write it:
181	
182	| Test | Split when... |
183	|------|--------------|
184	| "And"/"With" | Joins two verifiable things |
185	| Independent failure | Part A can pass while B fails |
186	| Scope words | "all", "every", "complete" → enumerate |
187	| Domain boundary | Crosses UI/API/data/logic → one per boundary |
188	| **No nameable probe** | You can't say which tool would verify it |
189	
190	**Format:** `- [ ] ISC-N: criterion text` — the criterion phrasing reveals its category. **All ISCs number sequentially as `ISC-N`** — anti-criteria included. ID-stability rule applies: never re-number on edit; splits become `ISC-N.M`.
191	
192	**Two doctrinal ISC kinds preserved as prose prefix conventions:**
193	
194	| Kind | Surface form | Rule |
195	|------|--------------|------|
196	| **Anti-criterion** — must NOT happen | `- [ ] ISC-N: Anti: <what must NOT happen>` | **≥1 required** |
197	| **Antecedent** — precondition for target experience | `- [ ] ISC-N: Antecedent: <precondition>` | **≥1 required when goal is experiential** |
198	
199	**For complex-app projects: the ISA test surface includes (non-exhaustive):**
200	- **Functional** — features work end-to-end
201	- **API** — endpoints exist, return expected shape, handle errors
202	- **Auth** — sign-in/out, token expiry, magic-link flow, session lifecycle
203	- **Authorization (RBAC/visibility)** — role X can/cannot reach endpoint Y
204	- **Performance** — latency budgets per route, bundle sizes, query times
205	- **Security model** — input validation, output encoding, CSRF, rate limits, secret handling
206	- **Data integrity** — schema invariants, foreign-key consistency, idempotency
207	- **Build & deploy** — `bun build` succeeds, typecheck clean, deploy version matches
208	- **Operational** — `/health` returns 200, error budget within SLO, synthetic monitor up
209	
210	These aren't "in addition to" the ISA — they ARE the ISA. The ISA is the test harness because the ISCs are the tests.
211	
212	**Allowed status markers:**
213	- `- [ ]` — pending, not yet verified
214	- `- [x]` — passed, verified with evidence
215	- `- [DEFERRED-VERIFY]` — passed in code/intent but live probe is impossible at execution time. **Requires a follow-up task ID in the verification notes.** Cannot be marked `[x]` until the deferred probe runs.

# Facts (durable memory)

Durable domain knowledge, data model, conventions, and settled decisions. The stable layer all
agents rely on. Update when a fact changes, not for daily activity.

## What AccessBuddy is
- Multi-tenant club access & credential management SaaS. Live at **https://accessbuddy.com.au**.
- Origin: rebuild of South Melbourne LSC (SMLSC) fob/building-access system (was Google Sheets +
  AppSheet + Apps Script) into a proper multi-tenant product. SMLSC is the first tenant; SMLSC's
  access hardware is **Integriti Inner Range**.
- Goal: commercialise for other surf lifesaving clubs and sports clubs.
- Business entity: Nicholas Wood Consulting Pty Ltd.

## Stack
- Frontend: Next.js (App Router). UI uses **shadcn on @base-ui/react** (NOT Radix).
- Backend: Bun + Hono. DB: Postgres (Drizzle ORM, migrations in `packages/db/drizzle`).
- Infra: GCP (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL Postgres 16), Stripe Connect, Firebase Auth, Resend (email),
  Sentry. CI/CD: GitHub Actions + release-please.

## Data model (settled)
- **Access level lives on the membership** (`tenantMemberships.accessLevelId`), NOT on the credential.
  The credential tracks status + expiry only. Integriti manages access at the member/card-holder
  level, not per-fob — a fob is just a physical token; permissions are on the person.
- Never create/deactivate credentials for an access-level change. Credential updates (expiry) use the
  `programmingRequired` flag directly on the credential, not the request pipeline.
- Orphaned-request fields exist in DB: `orphanEmail` / `orphanFirstName` / `orphanLastName`.

## Conventions (settled decisions)
- **Versioning:** `.release-please-manifest.json` is the source of truth (shown in UI footer + user
  menu). The `VERSION` file exists but is unused.
- **Branching:** `main` = production (auto-deploys), `dev` = working branch (commit here, PR to main).
- **Conventional commits matter for shipping:** release-please only cuts releases for
  `feat`/`fix`/`perf`/`revert`. `chore`/`docs`/`style`/`refactor`/`test`/`ci`/`build` merge but never
  deploy. Use `feat:`/`fix:` when a change must reach production.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` vars are Docker build args** (baked at build time), not runtime env. There are 8
  of them (see deploy workflow). Missing them → Firebase Auth / Stripe Elements / app URL silently
  undefined in the client bundle.
- **`gcloud run ... --set-env-vars` REPLACES all env vars** — use `--update-env-vars` to add one
  (replacing all once caused a prod outage).
- **base-ui Select:** render the selected label as explicit children of `SelectValue`; the
  `placeholder` prop alone won't show a selected value (common where value is a UUID).
- **Email quality:** always call `setEmailBranding()` with the tenant config before rendering any
  template; first-name-only in greetings; every email audit entry includes `subject` in metadata.
- **Stripe:** a `connect=true` webhook only receives connected-account events; platform-account
  payment intents need a separate platform webhook. AccessBuddy runs **dual webhooks** with the
  handler trying both `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `STRIPE_PLATFORM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- **Cloud Run custom domains are unavailable in australia-southeast1** — AccessBuddy uses a Global
  External Application Load Balancer (static IP 136.110.185.146, cert `accessbuddy-ssl`,
  NEG `accessbuddy-neg`).
- **Auto-migrations on deploy:** `entrypoint.sh` runs `bun run packages/db/src/migrate.ts` before the
  server starts. The Drizzle journal (`packages/db/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`) must list every
  migration file.

## Email system
- Event registry: 27 events in `@accessbuddy/shared/email-events.ts`.
- Per-tenant overrides via `email_configurations` table; block-based template editor; falls back to
  code defaults when no override exists.

# Facts (durable memory)

Durable domain knowledge, data model, conventions, and settled decisions. The stable layer all
agents rely on. Update when a fact changes, not for daily activity.

## What AccessBuddy is
- Multi-tenant club access & credential management SaaS. Live at **https://accessbuddy.com.au**.
- Origin: rebuild of South Melbourne LSC (SMLSC) fob/building-access system (was Google Sheets +
  AppSheet + Apps Script) into a proper multi-tenant product. SMLSC is the first tenant; SMLSC's
  access hardware is **Integriti Inner Range**.
- Goal: commercialise for other surf lifesaving clubs and sports clubs.
- Business entity: Nicholas Wood Consulting Pty Ltd.

## Stack
- Frontend: Next.js (App Router). UI uses **shadcn on @base-ui/react** (NOT Radix).
- Backend: Bun + Hono. DB: Postgres (Drizzle ORM, migrations in `packages/db/drizzle`).
- Infra: GCP (Cloud Run, Cloud SQL Postgres 16), Stripe Connect, Firebase Auth, Resend (email),
  Sentry. CI/CD: GitHub Actions + release-please.

## Data model (settled)
- **Access level lives on the membership** (`tenantMemberships.accessLevelId`), NOT on the credential.
  The credential tracks status + expiry only. Integriti manages access at the member/card-holder
  level, not per-fob — a fob is just a physical token; permissions are on the person.
- Never create/deactivate credentials for an access-level change. Credential updates (expiry) use the
  `programmingRequired` flag directly on the credential, not the request pipeline.
- Orphaned-request fields exist in DB: `orphanEmail` / `orphanFirstName` / `orphanLastName`.

## Conventions (settled decisions)
- **Versioning:** `.release-please-manifest.json` is the source of truth (shown in UI footer + user
  menu). The `VERSION` file exists but is unused.
- **Branching:** `main` = production (auto-deploys), `dev` = working branch (commit here, PR to main).
- **Conventional commits matter for shipping:** release-please only cuts releases for
  `feat`/`fix`/`perf`/`revert`. `chore`/`docs`/`style`/`refactor`/`test`/`ci`/`build` merge but never
  deploy. Use `feat:`/`fix:` when a change must reach production.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` vars are Docker build args** (baked at build time), not runtime env. There are 8
  of them (see deploy workflow). Missing them → Firebase Auth / Stripe Elements / app URL silently
  undefined in the client bundle.
- **`gcloud run ... --set-env-vars` REPLACES all env vars** — use `--update-env-vars` to add one
  (replacing all once caused a prod outage).
- **base-ui Select:** render the selected label as explicit children of `SelectValue`; the
  `placeholder` prop alone won't show a selected value (common where value is a UUID).
- **Email quality:** always call `setEmailBranding()` with the tenant config before rendering any
  template; first-name-only in greetings; every email audit entry includes `subject` in metadata.
- **Stripe:** a `connect=true` webhook only receives connected-account events; platform-account
  payment intents need a separate platform webhook. AccessBuddy runs **dual webhooks** with the
  handler trying both `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `STRIPE_PLATFORM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
- **Cloud Run custom domains are unavailable in australia-southeast1** — AccessBuddy uses a Global
  External Application Load Balancer (static IP 136.110.185.146, cert `accessbuddy-ssl`,
  NEG `accessbuddy-neg`).
- **Auto-migrations on deploy:** `entrypoint.sh` runs `bun run packages/db/src/migrate.ts` before the
  server starts. The Drizzle journal (`packages/db/drizzle/meta/_journal.json`) must list every
  migration file.

## Email system
- Event registry: 27 events in `@accessbuddy/shared/email-events.ts`.
- Per-tenant overrides via `email_configurations` table; block-based template editor; falls back to
  code defaults when no override exists.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/nicholas-wood/.claude/skills/Interceptor

## Customization

**Before executing, check for user customizations at:**
`~/.claude/PAI/USER/SKILLCUSTOMIZATIONS/Interceptor/`

If this directory exists, load and apply any PREFERENCES.md, configurations, or resources found there. These override default behavior. If the directory does not exist, proceed with skill defaults.


## MANDATORY: Voice Notification (REQUIRED BEFORE ANY ACTION)

**You MUST send this notification BEFORE doing anything else when this skill is invoked.**

1. **Send voice notification**:
   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST http://localhost:31337/notify \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"message": "Running the WORKFLOWNAME workflow in the Interceptor skill to ACTION"}' \
     > /dev/null 2>&1 &
   ```

2. **Output text notification**:
   ```
   Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **Interceptor** skill to ACTION...
   ```

**This is not optional. Execute this curl command immediately upon skill invocation.**

# Interceptor — Stealth Browser Automation

**Tool:** `interceptor` CLI — Chrome extension that controls the real browser from the inside.
**Repo:** https://github.com/Hacker-Valley-Media/slop-browser
**Install:** `~/Projects/interceptor` (built from source — see `Workflows/Update.md`)

### Why Interceptor?

agent-browser (the Browser skill) uses CDP — sites can detect it. Interceptor is a Chrome extension that operates through the actual browser UI. No debugger, no automation flags, no separate browser instance. You stay logged in, you pass bot detection, the agent sees what you see.

### Prerequisites

- Chrome or Brave running with the Interceptor extension loaded
- `interceptor` CLI in PATH (`/opt/homebrew/bin/interceptor`)
- `interceptor-daemon` in PATH (`/opt/homebrew/bin/interceptor-daemon`)
- Native messaging manifest registered (`bash ~/Projects/interceptor/scripts/install.sh --chrome --skip-extension`)
- (Optional, macOS) `interceptor-bridge` helper app — see "Bridge" section below

### Remote Execution — Linux box → Mac over SSH (REQUIRED on the Linux host)

Interceptor is a Chrome extension; it only runs where a real, logged-in Chrome
is. The Linux workstation has **no Chrome and no interceptor binary** — do not
try to install or run it locally there. Instead, drive the interceptor that
already lives on the Mac (where Nick stays logged into Seek, LinkedIn, etc.)
over SSH. The Mac is reachable as the `mac` / `nicholass-macbook-pro` SSH alias.

Prefix every interceptor command with the SSH hop and the Homebrew PATH (the
non-interactive SSH shell does not inherit `/opt/homebrew/bin`):

```bash
# Preflight: confirm the Mac, daemon, and Chrome are all up
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor status; pgrep -lf "Google Chrome" | head -1'

# Any interceptor command, run on the Mac's real browser:
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor open "https://www.seek.com.au/my-activity/saved-jobs" --text-only'
ssh mac 'export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH; interceptor scroll bottom; interceptor wait 1500; interceptor text | tail -90'
```

Wrap long output in `| head`/`| tail` to keep it bounded. Use `timeout 90 ssh …`
so a hung page can't stall the turn. Everything else in this skill works
unchanged once you've prefixed the SSH hop — refs, compound commands, network
log, scene graph all behave identically; they just execute on the Mac.

### Bridge — macOS Native Helper App

The bridge is an optional Swift helper that runs as a LaunchAgent and unlocks
capabilities the Chrome extension can't provide on its own: OS-level synthetic
input (`act --os`), accessibility tree of native macOS apps, app control,
clipboard, screen capture beyond Chrome, audio/speech, files, notifications,
HealthKit, Apple Intelligence. ~95% of typical work doesn't need it.

**Status check:** `interceptor status` reports `bridge: running` with PID + socket
when it's up, or `bridge: not running` when it isn't.

**Lifecycle (install / verify / troubleshoot / uninstall) lives entirely in
`Workflows/Update.md` section 6.** Future updates flow through the Update
workflow — never reach for the upstream `install-bridge.sh` directly; that
script breaks on Apple Silicon (`/usr/local/bin` needs sudo, but sudoing the
whole script makes `launchctl bootstrap` target uid 0 instead of the user).
The skill's procedure is the canonical one.

**Security model — read before installing:**

- Transport is a **UNIX domain socket** at `/tmp/interceptor-bridge.sock`.
  Local-only; no network listener; not reachable from another machine.
- **No authentication on the socket.** Any local process running as your user
  can connect and execute every bridge action — including synthetic input,
  clipboard read, audio capture, screenshots. macOS TCC permissions
  (Accessibility, Input Monitoring, Screen Recording, Microphone) are granted
  to the bridge once and inherited by every socket client.
- **Marginal risk is supply-chain:** a malicious package installed via
  bun/brew/npm gains a one-step path to OS-level input/screen/clipboard without
  needing its own permission grants — the bridge has them.
- Single-user Mac threat model: acceptable, since anything running as you can
  already do this with effort. Multi-user Macs need socket hardening (see
  Update.md section 6c).
- Binary built locally from `~/Projects/interceptor/interceptor-bridge/Sources/`,
  not a downloaded prebuilt. Provenance is Swift source we just compiled.

---

## Compound Commands (Preferred)

These collapse multi-step patterns into single invocations — fewer tool calls, fewer tokens:

```bash
interceptor open "https://example.com"              # Open URL, wait, return tree + text
interceptor open <url> --tree-only|--text-only|--full|--no-wait
interceptor read                                     # Tree + text for active tab
interceptor read <ref>                               # Tree + text for element subtree
interceptor read --include-style|--include-frames
interceptor act <ref>                                # Click + wait + return updated tree + diff
interceptor act <ref> "value"                        # Type + wait + return updated tree
interceptor act <ref> --os                           # OS-level trusted input (requires bridge)
interceptor act <ref> --keys "Enter"                 # Send keyboard shortcut
interceptor inspect                                  # Tree + text + network log + headers
interceptor inspect --net-only                       # Network only
```

## Core Commands

```bash
# State + discovery
interceptor state [--full]              # DOM tree + metadata
interceptor tree [--filter all] [--depth N] [--max-chars N]
interceptor diff                         # Changes since last state/tree read
interceptor find "query" [--role button] # Find elements by name
interceptor text [<index|ref>]
interceptor html <index|ref>

# Element interaction
interceptor click <ref>                  # Click by ref (eN)
interceptor click <ref> --at X,Y         # Click at coordinates
interceptor dblclick <ref> --at X,Y
interceptor rightclick <ref> --at X,Y
interceptor type <ref> <text> [--append]
interceptor type "role:name" <text>      # Semantic selector
interceptor select <ref> <value>         # Dropdown
interceptor focus|hover <ref>
interceptor drag <ref> --from X,Y --to X,Y [--steps N] [--duration MS]
interceptor keys "<combo>"               # e.g. "Control+A"

# Navigation + tabs
interceptor navigate <url>
interceptor back | forward
interceptor scroll <up|down|top|bottom>
interceptor wait <ms> | wait-stable [--ms N] [--timeout N]
interceptor tabs
interceptor tab new [url] | tab close [id] | tab switch <id>

# Capture
interceptor screenshot [--save] [--format png|jpeg] [--full] [--clip X,Y,W,H] [--element N]
interceptor eval <code> [--main]         # JS in isolated or main world
interceptor capture start | frame | stop # tabCapture stream

# Style injection (test redesigns live)
interceptor style inject --css "<rules>" [--top-only]
interceptor style remove <handle>

# Cookies
interceptor cookies <domain>
interceptor cookies set <json>
interceptor cookies delete <url> <name>
```

## Network

```bash
# Passive capture (always-on, no CDP fingerprint)
interceptor net log [--filter <pat>] [--limit N] [--since <ts>]
interceptor net headers [--filter <pat>]   # CSRF, auth headers
interceptor net clear

# Request override (passive, no CDP)
```

### Remote Execution — Linux box → Mac over SSH (REQUIRED on the Linux host)

Interceptor is a Chrome extension; it only runs where a real, logged-in Chrome
is. The Linux workstation has **no Chrome and no interceptor binary** — do not
try to install or run it locally there. Instead, drive the interceptor that
already lives on the Mac (where Nick stays logged into Seek, LinkedIn, etc.)

non-interactive SSH shell does not inherit `/opt/homebrew/bin`):


so a hung page can't stall the turn. Everything else in this skill works
unchanged once you've prefixed the SSH hop — refs, compound commands, network
log, scene graph all behave identically; they just execute on the Mac.

### Bridge — macOS Native Helper App

The bridge is an optional Swift helper that runs as a LaunchAgent and unlocks
capabilities the Chrome extension can't provide on its own: OS-level synthetic
input (`act --os`), accessibility tree of native macOS apps, app control,
clipboard, screen capture beyond Chrome, audio/speech, files, notifications,
HealthKit, Apple Intelligence. ~95% of typical work doesn't need it.

when it's up, or `bridge: not running` when it isn't.

workflow — never reach for the upstream `install-bridge.sh` directly; that
script breaks on Apple Silicon (`/usr/local/bin` needs sudo, but sudoing the

input.prompt:
Very thorough read-only exploration of the AccessBuddy monorepo at /home/nicholas-wood/Documents/workspace/projects/accessbuddy/code (Next.js App Router web app + Bun/Hono API + Postgres via Drizzle; packages under packages/, apps under apps/). Do NOT modify anything. Ignore node_modules.

Goal: I am about to add a new "Lockers" module (members request a changeroom locker; admins approve/decline, allocate a numbered locker, revoke; emails on allocate/decline/revoke; audit). It needs (a) a per-tenant feature flag that only a GLOBAL admin can toggle, (b) two NEW tenant-level permissions ("approve lockers" and "update/manage lockers") separate from existing ones. I need an exact map of the existing patterns to copy. Report file paths with line numbers and short quoted snippets for each of the following:

1. TENANT CONFIG / FEATURE FLAGS: where per-tenant settings live (table(s), columns, JSON config shape, zod schemas, defaults). In particular find the existing tenant flag `attestationAutoResend` and trace it end to end (schema, default, API read/write route, admin UI control). Is there any existing notion of per-tenant "features"/"modules" toggles?
2. GLOBAL ADMIN: how a global/platform admin is identified (column, helper function, middleware), which routes/pages are global-admin-only (e.g. tenant management pages), and where a global admin edits a tenant's config. Show the guard helper(s) and one example route + one example page.
3. PERMISSIONS / RBAC: the full permission model. Where permissions are enumerated (list every permission key), how they are stored (roles table? membership column? JSON?), how they are checked on API routes (helper name + example), how they are checked in the web UI/nav, and the admin UI where roles/permissions are assigned. Show how a recently added permission (e.g. "renew" or anything similar) was wired everywhere, so I can replicate for two new ones.
4. REQUEST WORKFLOW: the schema of the existing access/credential requests table(s) and status enums; the member-facing request submission flow (page + API route); the admin requests queue page + approve/decline routes. Include how public/unauthenticated vs authenticated members submit.
5. DB: location of Drizzle schema files, the migrations folder, the latest migration number/name, how migrations are generated (script names in package.json), the journal file, and how RLS policies / tenant_id scoping are written in migrations (show one recent migration that creates a tenant-scoped table with RLS if any). Also the DB access helper used in routes (e.g. withTenant / tenant-scoped db) with an example.
6. EMAIL: the email event registry (`email-events.ts`), how a new event + default template is added (files touched), `setEmailBranding`, the queue/send helper, and how attachments are (or are not) supported.
7. AUDIT LOG: how audit entries are written (helper + example), and where action labels are rendered (I'm told a new metadata.action needs labels in two renderers — find both).
8. WEB UI: the admin navigation definition (sidebar + mobile nav) and how items are conditionally shown by permission; the member-facing nav/home; the folder layout of apps/web routes (admin vs member vs global admin); the standard list page + detail page + dialog components used (give 2 representative files to copy).
9. TESTS: test runner(s), where API/unit tests live, how DB-backed tests get a database (embedded pg?), the commands to run typecheck, lint and tests (root package.json + turbo), and any CI workflow gates (.github/workflows).
10. Anything named or shaped like a "resource allocation" (numbered physical items assigned to members) that could be reused, and any seed/import scripts (scripts/ or data/) used to migrate SMLSC data from spreadsheets, since I will also write a one-off importer.

Also report: current git branch, whether the working tree is clean (`git status --short`), and the version in .release-please-manifest.json.

Return a structured report under those 10 headings, precise and concrete (paths:line, names, snippets). Flag anything surprising or inconsistent between patterns. Keep it under ~1800 words.

=========== feedback.md
# Feedback (collaboration patterns / learnings)

Project-specific ways of working: what to do, what to avoid, and why. Drawn from prior sessions.

## Collaboration with Nick
- **Present the user journey before coding.** Write a 3-5 step "admin clicks X, sees Y, system does Z"
  and confirm it first. Nick thinks in UX/workflow outcomes, not implementation. Going straight to
  code caused repeated UI rework (double-click approve, missing buttons, wrong labels, edit layout).
- **Rephrase requirements as user stories.** Nick describes outcomes, not mechanisms (e.g. "split the
  pickup step" meant "set pickup location while programming, but issue separately"). Restate as
  "When [role] does [action], they should see [result]" and confirm before coding — ambiguity has
  cost three rounds of fixes.
- **Ask about edge cases and existing data state first.** Nick tests with real-ish data (bulk fobs,
  deactivated credentials, multiple roles) and surfaces issues from data state you didn't consider
  (duplicate-key constraints, stale deactivated status, permission gating). Ask: current data state?
  which roles will test? what happens to existing records?
- **Design the full lifecycle before coding incrementally.** Map the complete happy path AND edge
  cases (reassignment, deactivated fobs, no rule match, permission checks) before the first line. The
  credential add endpoint took 5+ fix rounds because each fix revealed the next gap.
- **Rebase onto main and check conflicts before opening a PR;** verify PR state before claiming it's
  updated.

## Shipping / deploy (why these bit before)
- **Use `feat:`/`fix:` (not `chore:`) when a change must reach prod.** release-please skips chore/
  docs/etc, so a chore PR merges but never deploys. (Bit during cost-opt — needed a follow-up empty
  `fix:` commit.) Pure infra/docs that don't need a deploy can stay `chore:`.
- **`gcloud run ... --set-env-vars` REPLACES all env vars — use `--update-env-vars`.** `--set` once
  wiped DATABASE_URL and caused a prod outage. When unsure, `describe` the current env first.
- **Read the FULL `terraform plan` diff before apply.** gcloud-based CI drift can roll the image back
  to `:latest` or strip env vars (`STRIPE_PLATFORM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN`). Verify
  `lifecycle.ignore_changes` is still on the Cloud Run resource; add missing env vars to TF before
  applying; scope with `-target` when in doubt.
- **`NEXT_PUBLIC_*` must be Docker build args.** Missing them → Firebase Auth / Stripe Elements / app
  URL silently undefined in the client bundle (cost 30 min to trace once).

## Quality bars Nick has flagged repeatedly
- **Emails:** always `setEmailBranding()` before rendering; first-name-only greetings; test with
  tenant colours before calling an email feature done.
- **Audit log:** every email audit entry must carry `subject` in metadata, and the display must render
  it (not a bare "Email Sent").
- **base-ui Select:** render selected label as explicit children of `SelectValue` (placeholder alone
  won't show a UUID-keyed value).

## Domain gotcha
- **Access level is on the membership, not the credential.** Don't create/deactivate credentials for
=========== feedback_accessbuddy_collaboration.md
---
name: AccessBuddy collaboration learnings
description: Retrospective findings from 31 March - 2 April AccessBuddy sessions on how to collaborate better with Nick
type: feedback
---

Present user journeys before coding - "the admin clicks X, sees Y, the system does Z." Nick thinks in terms of user experience and workflow outcomes, not implementation details. When I go straight to code without describing the experience, I miss UX issues that require rework.

**Why:** Multiple rounds of UI fixes (approve double-click, missing buttons, wrong labels, edit form layout) could have been caught by describing the interaction before building it.

**How to apply:** Before implementing any UI-facing feature, write a 3-5 step user journey and present it. For data model decisions, present options with implications rather than assuming.

---

Ask about edge cases and existing data state before implementing. Nick tests with real-ish data (bulk-added fobs, deactivated credentials, multiple user roles) and catches issues that arise from data state I didn't consider.

**Why:** Duplicate key constraints, stale deactivated status, permission gating issues all came from not considering the existing data and role context.

**How to apply:** Before implementing, ask: "What's the current state of the data I'll be working with? What roles will test this? What happens to existing records?"

---

Nick describes outcomes, not mechanisms. When he says "split the pickup step," he means "let the admin set the pickup location at the same time as programming, but issue separately." When requirements feel ambiguous, rephrase them back as a user story before proceeding.

**Why:** Misinterpreting "split pickup" caused three rounds of fixes. The word "split" was ambiguous - it could mean separate or combine depending on perspective.

**How to apply:** Rephrase every requirement as "When [role] does [action], they should see [result]" and confirm before coding.

---

Design the full lifecycle before coding incrementally. The credential add endpoint had 5+ fix rounds because each fix revealed the next gap. Map the complete happy path AND edge cases (reassignment, deactivated fobs, no rule match, permission checks) before writing the first line.

**Why:** Incremental fixes to the credential lifecycle were more expensive than designing it properly upfront would have been.

**How to apply:** For any workflow or lifecycle feature, write out every state transition and what changes at each step before implementing.
=========== feedback_accessbuddy_datamodel.md
---
name: AccessBuddy Data Model
description: Access level on membership not credential. Credential tracks status and expiry only.
type: feedback
---

Access level lives on the membership (tenantMemberships.accessLevelId), not the credential. The credential tracks status and expiry only. When programming an access update in Integriti, the programmer updates the member, not the individual fob. The fob is not replaced for access level changes.

**Why:** The access control system (Integriti Inner Range) manages access at the member/card-holder level, not per-fob. A fob is just a physical token - the access permissions are on the person.

**How to apply:** Never create/deactivate credentials for access level changes. Credential updates (expiry) use `programmingRequired` flag directly on the credential, not the request pipeline.
=========== feedback_email_audit_quality.md
---
name: Email and Audit Quality Standards
description: Always apply tenant branding to emails and include subject/context in audit entries. Recurring frustration point.
type: feedback
---

When building email features, ALWAYS ensure tenant branding is applied via setEmailBranding() before rendering templates. When adding audit log entries for emails, ALWAYS include the subject line in metadata. Both issues have been flagged multiple times.

**Why:** Nick has had to call out email formatting and audit log context issues repeatedly. The daily summary email shipped without tenant branding, and audit entries for emails showed bare "Email Sent" without subjects. These are basic quality expectations.

**How to apply:**
- Before calling any email template function, call `setEmailBranding()` with the tenant's config
- All email audit entries must include `subject` in metadata (already in sendEmail, but custom sends must match)
- Audit log display components must render email subject when action is email_sent/email_failed
- Use first name only in email greetings (split on space, take first element)
- Test email rendering with tenant-specific colours before considering an email feature complete
=========== feedback_select_label_pattern.md
---
name: Select Component Label Pattern
description: base-ui Select requires explicit children in SelectValue to show label, not just placeholder prop
type: feedback
---

When using the shadcn/base-ui Select in AccessBuddy, the `SelectValue` component must render the selected label explicitly via children, not rely on `placeholder` prop alone. The `label` prop on `SelectItem` does not reliably propagate to the trigger display.

**Why:** The project uses `@base-ui/react/select` (not Radix). The `SelectValue` `placeholder` only shows when nothing is selected. The selected item's display text must be rendered as children of `SelectValue` using a lookup like `items.find(i => i.id === selectedId)?.name`.

**How to apply:** Every `SelectValue` in queue-item, admin-actions, or any component where value !== display text must use the explicit children pattern:
```tsx
<SelectValue>
  {selectedId ? items.find(i => i.id === selectedId)?.name ?? "Select..." : "Select..."}
</SelectValue>
```
Never use just `<SelectValue placeholder="Select..." />` when the value is a UUID.

=========== feedback_accessbuddy_collaboration.md
---
name: AccessBuddy collaboration learnings
description: Retrospective findings from 31 March - 2 April AccessBuddy sessions on how to collaborate better with Nick
type: feedback
---

Present user journeys before coding - "the admin clicks X, sees Y, the system does Z." Nick thinks in terms of user experience and workflow outcomes, not implementation details. When I go straight to code without describing the experience, I miss UX issues that require rework.

**Why:** Multiple rounds of UI fixes (approve double-click, missing buttons, wrong labels, edit form layout) could have been caught by describing the interaction before building it.

**How to apply:** Before implementing any UI-facing feature, write a 3-5 step user journey and present it. For data model decisions, present options with implications rather than assuming.

---

Ask about edge cases and existing data state before implementing. Nick tests with real-ish data (bulk-added fobs, deactivated credentials, multiple user roles) and catches issues that arise from data state I didn't consider.

**Why:** Duplicate key constraints, stale deactivated status, permission gating issues all came from not considering the existing data and role context.

**How to apply:** Before implementing, ask: "What's the current state of the data I'll be working with? What roles will test this? What happens to existing records?"

---

Nick describes outcomes, not mechanisms. When he says "split the pickup step," he means "let the admin set the pickup location at the same time as programming, but issue separately." When requirements feel ambiguous, rephrase them back as a user story before proceeding.

**Why:** Misinterpreting "split pickup" caused three rounds of fixes. The word "split" was ambiguous - it could mean separate or combine depending on perspective.

**How to apply:** Rephrase every requirement as "When [role] does [action], they should see [result]" and confirm before coding.

---

Design the full lifecycle before coding incrementally. The credential add endpoint had 5+ fix rounds because each fix revealed the next gap. Map the complete happy path AND edge cases (reassignment, deactivated fobs, no rule match, permission checks) before writing the first line.

**Why:** Incremental fixes to the credential lifecycle were more expensive than designing it properly upfront would have been.

**How to apply:** For any workflow or lifecycle feature, write out every state transition and what changes at each step before implementing.
=========== feedback_accessbuddy_datamodel.md
---
name: AccessBuddy Data Model
description: Access level on membership not credential. Credential tracks status and expiry only.
type: feedback
---

Access level lives on the membership (tenantMemberships.accessLevelId), not the credential. The credential tracks status and expiry only. When programming an access update in Integriti, the programmer updates the member, not the individual fob. The fob is not replaced for access level changes.

**Why:** The access control system (Integriti Inner Range) manages access at the member/card-holder level, not per-fob. A fob is just a physical token - the access permissions are on the person.

**How to apply:** Never create/deactivate credentials for access level changes. Credential updates (expiry) use `programmingRequired` flag directly on the credential, not the request pipeline.
=========== feedback_email_audit_quality.md
---
name: Email and Audit Quality Standards
description: Always apply tenant branding to emails and include subject/context in audit entries. Recurring frustration point.
type: feedback
---

When building email features, ALWAYS ensure tenant branding is applied via setEmailBranding() before rendering templates. When adding audit log entries for emails, ALWAYS include the subject line in metadata. Both issues have been flagged multiple times.

**Why:** Nick has had to call out email formatting and audit log context issues repeatedly. The daily summary email shipped without tenant branding, and audit entries for emails showed bare "Email Sent" without subjects. These are basic quality expectations.

**How to apply:**
- Before calling any email template function, call `setEmailBranding()` with the tenant's config
- All email audit entries must include `subject` in metadata (already in sendEmail, but custom sends must match)
- Audit log display components must render email subject when action is email_sent/email_failed
- Use first name only in email greetings (split on space, take first element)
- Test email rendering with tenant-specific colours before considering an email feature complete
=========== feedback_select_label_pattern.md
---
name: Select Component Label Pattern
description: base-ui Select requires explicit children in SelectValue to show label, not just placeholder prop
type: feedback
---

When using the shadcn/base-ui Select in AccessBuddy, the `SelectValue` component must render the selected label explicitly via children, not rely on `placeholder` prop alone. The `label` prop on `SelectItem` does not reliably propagate to the trigger display.

**Why:** The project uses `@base-ui/react/select` (not Radix). The `SelectValue` `placeholder` only shows when nothing is selected. The selected item's display text must be rendered as children of `SelectValue` using a lookup like `items.find(i => i.id === selectedId)?.name`.

**How to apply:** Every `SelectValue` in queue-item, admin-actions, or any component where value !== display text must use the explicit children pattern:
```tsx
<SelectValue>
  {selectedId ? items.find(i => i.id === selectedId)?.name ?? "Select..." : "Select..."}
</SelectValue>
```
Never use just `<SelectValue placeholder="Select..." />` when the value is a UUID.

<result>I've mapped all 10 areas. A few things you assumed don't match the code, and one looks like a live security bug, so those come first.

**Corrections to your assumptions**
- **There is no Bun/Hono API app.** `apps/` contains only `web`. Every API route is a Next.js route handler under `apps/web/src/app/api/v1/t/[slug]/…` (tenant routes) and `apps/web/src/app/api/v1/platform/…` (platform routes). Packages are `packages/db` and `packages/shared`.
- **`attestationAutoResend` has no write route and no admin UI control.** It only exists in the schema (`packages/shared/src/schemas.ts:181`) and is read by the cron (`apps/web/src/app/api/cron/daily/route.ts:269`).
- **There is no per-tenant "features"/"modules" toggle anywhere, and no place where a global admin edits a tenant's config.** Global admins use the same tenant settings page as club admins.
- **No embedded Postgres for tests.** DB-backed tests need a real database via `DATABASE_URL`.

**Repo state:** branch `fix/member-page-reload-after-confirmation-actions`, `git status --short` shows nothing (clean), `.release-please-manifest.json` is `"1.23.3"`.

## 1. Tenant config / feature flags
- **Storage:** `packages/db/src/schema/tenants.ts:15`: `settings: jsonb("settings").$type<TenantSettings>().notNull().default(sql\`'{}'::jsonb\`)`.
- **Schema and defaults:** `tenantSettingsSchema` at `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts:160-206`. The flag is at `:181`: `attestationAutoResend: z.boolean().default(true)`. Booleans that work like flags today: `sendEmails`, `splitPickupFromProgramming`, `allowFobCreationAtProgramming`, `allowSelfServiceLostReport`.
- **Defaults are not applied on read.** Stored JSON is never parsed through the schema, so every reader handles `undefined` itself. Examples: `lib/attestation-resend-logic.ts:32` ("undefined is treated as enabled"), `lib/services/email.ts` `buildEmailConfig` (`s.sendEmails === undefined ? true : …`), and the `TenantSettings` type at `schemas.ts:208-214`.
- **Read/write route:** `apps/web/src/app/api/v1/t/[slug]/config/settings/route.ts`.
  - GET needs `VIEW` (`:20`). PUT needs `CONFIGURE` (`:106`).
  - PUT shallow-merges the body into existing settings: `updates.settings = { ...tenant.settings, ...settings }` (`:54`).
  - It writes a `settings_update` audit entry with a `changes` diff (`:86-98`).
- **⚠ The PUT accepts any key.** Its body schema ends in `.passthrough()` (`:23-34`), so anyone with `CONFIGURE` can set any settings key, including a future locker flag. The settings page also sends back the whole settings object (`admin/config/settings/page.tsx:116`: `...data?.settings`). A global-admin-only flag therefore has to be stripped or preserved server-side in this route; hiding it in the UI is not enough.
- **UI checkbox pattern to copy:** `apps/web/src/app/t/[slug]/admin/config/settings/page.tsx` — state at `:50/:63`, load at `:77`, save body at `:109-129`, checkbox cards at `:501-515` and `:565-583`.

- **How it's identified:** a row in `admin_assignments` with `role_type='global_admin'` and `tenant_id=NULL`. Created at `app/api/v1/platform/global-admins/route.ts:86-92`. The table is defined at `packages/db/src/schema/memberships.ts` (`adminAssignments`, around `:50-70`).
- **Helper:** `isGlobalAdmin(auth)` at `apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:122`. `checkPermission` grants everything to global admins (`lib/permissions.ts:27-32`).
- **There is no middleware.** Each handler checks inline. Example route `app/api/v1/platform/tenants/route.ts:18`:
  ```ts
  if (!isGlobalAdmin(auth)) return NextResponse.json({ error: "Global admin access required" }, { status: 403 });
  ```
- **Example page guard:** `app/admin/layout.tsx:14-17` (`if (!isGlobalAdmin(auth)) redirect("/")`). It covers `/admin/tenants`, `/admin/landing`, `/admin/global-admins` and `/admin/logins`.
- `app/admin/tenants/page.tsx` links each tenant to `/t/{slug}/admin/config/settings`. The platform tenants API only supports GET (list) and POST (create, name+slug); there is no PATCH. You'll need a new platform route, e.g. `PATCH /api/v1/platform/tenants/[id]`.
- `app/t/[slug]/admin/tenants/page.tsx` is a near-duplicate of the platform tenants page and is not in any nav; it looks like a leftover.

content.text:
━━━ 📃 SUMMARY ━━━ 7/7

🔄 ITERATION on: Adding the legacy locker script into AccessBuddy with a per-tenant flag and separate approve/update permissions.

📃 CONTENT:

**Nothing is built yet. I have the design ready and need you to confirm the journey before I code**, per your standing AccessBuddy rule.

**Inputs**
- **Script:** the Downloads export is byte-identical to a June checkout already in the workspace, so I read it from there. clasp's Google login on the Mac has expired, and the Interceptor Chrome profile isn't signed into Google, so I could not read the live editor.
- **Spreadsheet:** two changerooms of 42 lockers each, 14 marked single use, 29 current allocations, 6 pending requests, 1 revoked, 2 approvers.

**What the legacy script does**
1. A Google Form submission becomes a request with an optional preferred locker number.
2. The script proposes a locker: the preferred one if free, otherwise the middle of the longest empty run.
3. An approver allocates it. The member gets an email with the locker policy attached, and the locker is flagged "sticker update required".
4. Decline sends an email with a reason.
5. Revoke clears the locker, emails the member a 7-day notice to remove belongings, and flags the sticker.

**Proposed journey in AccessBuddy**
1. **Global admin** turns on "Lockers" for a tenant from the platform Tenants page. Club admins cannot see or change it.
2. **Member** (signed in, active membership) sees "Request a locker" on their dashboard, picks an area, optionally a preferred number, and accepts the locker policy.
3. **Approver** sees a Lockers tab with pending requests, each showing the suggested locker. They can change the number, then Approve (which allocates and emails) or Decline with a reason.
4. **Locker manager** sees the grid of lockers per area. They can revoke with a reason, move a member, mark a locker single use or out of service, add or remove lockers, and tick off the sticker to-do list.
5. **Member** sees their locker on the dashboard. Every action is written to the audit log.

**Permissions**
- **Approve lockers:** approve or decline requests.
- **Update lockers:** revoke, move, edit the locker inventory, clear sticker flags.
- Club admins and global admins get both, as with every other permission.

**Things the code forces**
- The tenant settings save route accepts any key, so the flag must be protected server-side and set through a new global-admin-only route. Hiding it in the UI would not be enough.
- There is no existing "modules" concept; this will be the first.
- Queued emails cannot carry attachments, so locker emails with the policy attached must send directly.

**Pre-existing risk, confirmed and not touched**
`buildAuthContext` in `apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts:296` joins admin roles to memberships on user only, not tenant. An admin of club A who is a member of club B would carry A's permissions into B. It is harmless with one tenant but must be fixed before a second.

**Decisions for you** (my recommendation in each)
1. **Approve and allocate in one step?** Recommend yes. The sheet shows both always done seconds apart by the same person.
2. **Does revoke sit under "Update lockers"?** Recommend yes, so approvers cannot remove lockers.
3. **Who can request?** Recommend signed-in active members only, replacing the form's "are you financial?" self-declaration. The alternative is a public form like fob requests.
4. **Limit of one locker per member?** Recommend no hard limit, with a warning to the approver if the member already holds one.
5. **Import the SMLSC data?** Recommend yes: I build an importer with a dry-run report matching sheet emails to members, and you approve the production run separately.
6. **Fix the cross-tenant role join now?** Recommend a separate small PR, not bundled with lockers.

Defaults I'll take unless you object: no fees, no seasonal expiry, generic "locker areas" rather than hard-coded male/female, and a tenant-uploaded policy document.

🖊️ STORY:
- Locker logic lived in a spreadsheet script.
- I read the script, data and codebase.
- Design is ready; the code is not started.
- Your answers on six decisions unlock the build.

🗣️ Jarvis: Lockers design ready; confirm the journey and six decisions before I build.

=========== project-accessbuddy-pr125-force-renew-staging.md
---
name: project-accessbuddy-pr125-force-renew-staging
description: "AccessBuddy PR #125 (3 Nov 2026): Force Renew used to rewrite expiresAt on active fobs and skip expired ones, never flagging the programmer; now stages like the attestation yes-path. Christine Cardwell was the trigger; her fob is expired so re-running Force Renew after release stages it."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 2e24043d-57c6-4e57-bc9b-ac59de31bfef
  modified: 2026-11-03T05:27:04.990Z
---

Force Renew (`members/[id]/force-renew/route.ts`) dated from 31 Mar 2026 and was never migrated to the 8 Apr staged-expiry model: it wrote `expiresAt` straight onto ACTIVE fobs and ignored EXPIRED ones, so nothing ever set `programmingRequired`, the only filter on `/admin` credential updates. Trigger: Nick, 3 Nov 2026, "Force renew was done today for Christine Cardwell, but her fob was not sent for expiry update". Prod logs: one force-renew POST 00:28Z, the only one in 30 days. The 4 Sep Dinah Boswell review had already recorded the defect (state.md item 8) and three members force-renewed 2-3 Sep; it sat unactioned.

Fix on branch `fix/force-renew-stages-expiry-update` (895a8ae), PR https://github.com/nicholas-wood/accessbuddy/pull/125 (merged 3 Nov on Nick's instruction, release PR #126 → v1.23.3 live 05:49Z, health 200), ISC-181..203 in the project ISA: stages `pendingExpiresAt` + `programmingRequired` for active and expired fobs via `scopedAttestationExpiry`, skips a fob already at the target or already staged for it, keeps the reason on an already-flagged fob, completes every pending attestation (guarded on `pending`), returns `staged`/`skipped`, labels in both audit renderers, form copy fixed. DB-gated `force-renew.test.ts` (9 cases).

**Why:** the programmer only sees the staged flag; a direct expiry write leaves AccessBuddy claiming a date the door system never got.

**How to apply:**
- v1.23.3 is live. Re-run Force Renew on the member (her fob is `expired`, so the old code did nothing to it) and probe `/admin` with Interceptor (ISC-202).
- Pre-release workaround that needs no deploy: Add Credential → her expired fob under "This member's previous fobs" → expiry-update stage → "Member confirmed in person" stages it immediately.
- Old-route rows: `force_renew_expiry_update` audit rows with `newExpiresAt` and no `pendingExpiresAt` mark active fobs that were rewritten but never programmed; the new skip rule leaves them alone. Probe SQL at `projects/accessbuddy/artifacts/sql/2026-11-03-force-renew-probe.sql` (Q2) for Nick's DB window.
- Embedded test Postgres: `/tmp/ab-pg-scratch` was wiped by tmp cleanup while its server kept running on an empty data dir (tests "pass" with every DB suite skipped). Rebuilt at `~/.claude/jobs/2e24043d/tmp/ab-pg/run.ts` (`bun add embedded-postgres@17.5.0-beta.15`, then `bun pm trust --all` or initdb exits 127). Always check "0 skipped" and that `ss -ltn | grep 54329` is backed by a live data dir. See [[project-accessbuddy-pr111-expiry-update-stage]].
- Refactor still owed: attestation yes-path, confirm-on-behalf, manual stage and force-renew each inline the same staging block; a shared `stageExpiryUpdate(tx, …)` helper would have prevented this class of drift (RCA root cause).
- Follow-ups 3 Nov: PR #127 (chore) renames the member-page card Attestations → Confirmations; PR #128 (fix) reloads the page after Force Renew / re-send / confirmation actions because a soft refresh left the cards stale for Nick (RSC fetch did fire; cause unproven, Interceptor unreachable from bg). Other components on the page still soft-refresh.
- 8 Nov: #127 and #128 merged (128 rebased onto 127 cleanly), release PR #129 → v1.23.4 live after three reruns of the Release Please deploy; the first two attempts died in setup-bun with GitHub 504s downloading Bun 1.4.4 (infrastructure, not code). Gotcha: `gh pr merge` succeeded on #128 despite a failed Build check, so branch protection does not require Build; `gh run rerun <id> --failed` is the recovery.
=========== gotcha-accessbuddy-prod-access.md
---
name: gotcha-accessbuddy-prod-access
description: How to reach AccessBuddy prod (GCP/DB/Resend/gh) from the Linux box — everything goes via the Mac
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: ef252aad-8fb2-47d8-b675-f77609c21d47
  modified: 2026-09-20T01:52:13.061Z
---

AccessBuddy prod access from the Linux box, all via `ssh mac` (nothing installed locally):

- **gcloud**: `/opt/homebrew/bin/gcloud` (Homebrew — bare `ssh mac gcloud` fails, non-interactive PATH misses it). Authenticated as nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com. Project `accessbuddy-prod`, service `accessbuddy-production`, region australia-southeast1.
- **Prod DB**: Cloud SQL private-IP only. Pattern: `gcloud sql instances patch --assign-ip` → `cloud-sql-proxy` (also in /opt/homebrew/bin) on port 5433 → psql at `/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/bin/psql` → `--no-assign-ip` and VERIFY `ipv4Enabled: False` after. DATABASE_URL is a literal env var on the Cloud Run service (read via `gcloud run services describe`, never print the password). `audit_log` is FORCE RLS — `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', ...)` first; SMLSC tenant slug is `south-melb-lsc` (not `smlsc`).
- **Resend keys are send-only restricted** (401 on all read/management endpoints) — forensics needs a temp full-access key from the dashboard, revoked after.
- **gh**: `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`, token lives in the macOS keychain (locked over SSH) — use `GH_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.gh-token)` (file Nick exports from his GUI terminal). No gh and no token on the Linux box, but git push over SSH works there.
- **Merging without gh (verified 4 Sep 2026, v1.16.0):** `git merge --no-ff feature && git push origin main` lands the feature; release-please then refreshes `origin/release-please--branches--main` within ~30s; `git merge --ff-only` that branch into main and push. GitHub auto-marks the release PR merged, release-please cuts the tag/release within a minute, and the deploy job runs (release → live site ≈ 11-12 min). Probe: `curl -s https://accessbuddy.com.au/ | rg -o "1\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]"` shows the deployed version.
- **Postgres RLS flags**: `forcerowsecurity` is NOT in pg_tables — use `pg_class.relforcerowsecurity` (this wrong-column mistake was made twice in Aug 2026).
- Complex ssh one-liners with nested quotes break silently and can leave the IP window open — always ship a script file via scp instead, with the IP disable inside it, and verify the flag after.
- The Mac drops off Tailscale for 10-30 min at a time (Sept 2026: three dropouts in one hour). Run pulls from a background retry loop, write the script's output to a file on the Mac (`nohup … > ~/pai-tmp/x.out`) then cat it, so a dropped link cannot lose it, and re-check `ipv4Enabled` after any run whose SSH session died mid-flight.
- **IP-window scripts can leave prod exposed for hours (12 Sep 2026):** the open-query-close script's cleanup (`--no-assign-ip`) needs network; the Mac dropped off Tailscale mid-run and the window stayed open from 15:52 to 19:58 Melbourne before cleanup completed. Put a hard `timeout` on the psql step and run the close as its own retry loop, and always re-check `ipv4Enabled` after any run that overlapped a dropout.
- In this bg-job session (12 Sep 2026) gcloud read-only and scheduler create/update/run over `ssh mac` were all allowed; only earlier `sql instances patch` shapes were denied. Nick launching the DB script via `!` is still the reliable path.
- **Login forensics without the DB (20 Sep 2026, Belinda Porter "can't log in"):** three read-only probes over `ssh mac` were all allowed in a bg job and carried the diagnosis. (1) `gcloud logging read` on `httpRequest.requestUrl:"/api/auth/"`, then filter by `httpRequest.remoteIp` to rebuild a person's session page by page (request logs carry no email; `/t/<slug>/admin` hits vs `/` tells you whether they got in). (2) Firebase Auth last-login: `curl -X POST https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/projects/accessbuddy-prod/accounts:lookup` with `Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)`, header `x-goog-user-project: accessbuddy-prod`, body `{"email":[...]}` gives createdAt / lastLoginAt / lastRefreshAt / disabled. (3) `textPayload:"<name>"` search finds contact-form payloads. Known dead end: a magic-link sign-in for an address with no admin assignment or membership succee
- Renewal forensics: "renewed" on the member page means only that an admin clicked Renew; check `attestation_requests.status` and `credentials.programming_required` before reasoning about the daily summary.
- **Shipping from a bg job (16 Sep 2026, v1.18.1):** the auto-mode classifier denies `git merge` + `git push origin main` as publication. What works: push the feature branch from Linux, then `ssh mac 'export GH_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.gh-token) && /opt/homebrew/bin/gh pr create --repo nicholas-wood/accessbuddy --base main --head <branch> ...'`, watch with `gh pr checks <n> --watch` (the Mac has no `timeout` command), and leave the merge to Nick. DB-gated tests only run in CI, so check FK delete order in afterAll (PROGRAM creates a credential that references the request).
=========== project-accessbuddy-pr111-expiry-update-stage.md
---
name: project-accessbuddy-pr111-expiry-update-stage
description: "AccessBuddy PR #111 (open 18 Oct 2026) adds an expiry_update stage to Add Credential for a fob the member already holds; staged via pendingExpiresAt + programmingRequired, no request; QA found two blockers fixed in commit 2; live Interceptor probe deferred"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 3895ea31-b902-4050-8e28-cfbee513d73e
  modified: 2026-10-18T09:18:03.143Z
---

PR https://github.com/nicholas-wood/accessbuddy/pull/111, branch `feat/add-fob-reissue-expiry` in worktree `.worktrees/fob-reissue` (two commits: e63b7bd feature, then the QA-round fix). Nick's ask: "when I add a fob, I need an option to put it into the update expiry flow (they already have the fob, it is just expired and had been removed from the member previously)". ISC-106..144 in the project ISA.

Design that shipped: fourth stage `expiry_update` on `POST /credentials` (function `stageExpiryUpdate` in `credentials/route.ts`). Re-attaches the existing (tenant,type,serial) row to the member, forces `status: expired`, stages `pendingExpiresAt` (membership-year default for everyone, past dates refused), `programmingRequired` + reason naming serial and previous deactivation reason, no `fob_requests` row, audit `manual_expiry_update` with a snapshot. The UNCHANGED confirm-programming route then reactivates and emails `credentialReactivated`. Refusals are a typed `ManualAddRefused` → 400 (the wrapper otherwise returns a bare 500). Member page offers the member's own expired/returned fobs under "This member's previous fobs" only for this stage.

**Why:** "update expiry flow" in this codebase is the staged-expiry path, not a request type; forcing `expired` is what `resolveConfirmProgramming` reactivates from, so no downstream route changed and no migration was needed.

**How to apply:**
- Merge is Nick's. After release: Interceptor probe (ISC-142) on an SMLSC member page: fourth stage, own-fob group, stage one, row on `/admin` credential updates, audit line "Re-added to member - expiry update staged for …".
- Another session's branch in the main checkout also edits `packages/shared/src/schemas.ts` and `audit-trail.tsx`; second to merge rebases.
- Decisions Nick may want to overturn (in the PR body): no payment for this stage; cancel-programming leaves the fob on the member; revoked (free-text reason) fobs are eligible with the reason surfaced.
- Lesson: a background typecheck started before the last file is written proves nothing; the QA agent caught a TS error in the test file after I had claimed "typecheck clean". Run the gate on the final tree with `--force`.
- Lesson: the embedded test Postgres wrapper (`/tmp/ab-pg-scratch/run.ts`) can be alive while the server is shut down; `bun run test` then reports green with 68 DB-gated tests silently skipped. Check `ss -ltn | grep 54329` and "0 skipped" before trusting a baseline. See [[project-accessbuddy-pr106-old-fob-retirement]] for the recipe.

**Follow-up 19 Oct 2026 (branch `feat/expiry-update-member-confirm`, Nick: "the member should have to confirm they have it first"):** the stage no longer flags the programmer. It re-attaches the row (expired, deactivation fields kept) and raises a SCOPED renewal attestation (`attestation_requests.credential_ids`, migration 0020) emailing `credentialHeldConfirmation`; the attest page lists only that fob; "yes" stages the season expiry + programmingRequired (quoting the old deactivation reason), "no" leaves the fob expired, logs "Member confirmed they no longer have the fob. Member must submit a new request", and the page tells the member to submit a new request (Nick's call, 19 Oct); weekly auto-resend capped at 4; admin Re-send / Cancel confirmation / Member confirmed in person on the member page (`cancel-confirmation`, `confirm-on-behalf` routes). QA caught two highs before merge: scope

**Post-deploy defect 19 Oct:** "went straight to programming" = the form's preselected "Send for Programming" stage with a previously revoked fob (production request log: the add call created a request; the expiry-update path never does). Fix PR #119 merged (afd58eb) and released as v1.23.1 (live 23 Oct): no default stage, previously-held fob auto-selects expiry-update. Diagnosis tip that worked without the DB or Interceptor: `gcloud logging read` on `httpRequest.requestUrl:"/t/<slug>/"` around the POST shows the page the admin landed on and any new ids the refreshed page prefetched.

**23 Oct follow-up:** after cancelling the mis-staged request the fob was `pending_programming`, unowned, and carried a phantom deactivation flag (pre-existing: CANCEL flags any non-deactivated credential even if never programmed), and the expiry-update stage refused `pending_programming`. Fix PR #121 merged (35e1977), released v1.23.2 (live 23 Oct): never-programmed cancel only unallocates; `pending_programming` eligible when unowned/own. Lesson: when adding a status allow-list on a re-add path, walk every state the request lifecycle can leave a credential in (cancel before PROGRAM leaves `pending_programming`).
=========== gotcha-accessbuddy-vitest-tsx-render-probe.md
---
name: gotcha-accessbuddy-vitest-tsx-render-probe
description: AccessBuddy's default vitest config cannot transform TSX (tsconfig jsx preserve); verify UI copy with a throwaway config that sets esbuild.jsx automatic and renderToString
metadata:
  type: reference
---

AccessBuddy `apps/web` has `"jsx": "preserve"` in tsconfig, so `bunx vitest run` chokes on any `.tsx` test (and a stray `.tsx` test file makes the default suite report failures). To verify member-facing copy as rendered HTML without a browser: export the component, write a throwaway `zz-vitest.render.config.ts` inside `apps/web` (must live in the repo so `vitest/config` resolves) with `esbuild: { jsx: "automatic" }`, `test.include` pointing at a `zz-*.test.tsx` under `src/__tests__/`, and the `@` alias; run `bunx vitest run --config zz-vitest.render.config.ts`; assert on `renderToString(...)` output; delete both files before committing. Used 2026-09-06 for the expired-fob notice on the request form.

**How to apply:** when a UI change needs copy or role verification and Interceptor on the Mac is unavailable, use this probe instead of claiming from source. Related: [[gotcha-accessbuddy-prod-access]] (gh via `GH_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.gh-token)` on the Mac worked again for PR #96).

AccessBuddy `apps/web` has `"jsx": "preserve"` in tsconfig, so `bunx vitest run` chokes on any `.tsx` test (and a stray `.tsx` test file makes the default suite report failures). Used 2026-09-06 for the expired-fob notice on the request form.

Force Renew (`members/[id]/force-renew/route.ts`) dated from 31 Mar 2026 and was never migrated to the 8 Apr staged-expiry model: it wrote `expiresAt` straight onto ACTIVE fobs and ignored EXPIRED ones, so nothing ever set `programmingRequired`, the only filter on `/admin` credential updates. Trigger: Nick, 3 Nov 2026, "Force renew was done today for Christine Cardwell, but her fob was not sent for expiry update". Prod logs: one force-renew POST 00:28Z, the only one in 30 days. The 4 Sep Dinah Boswell review had already recorded the defect (state.md item 8) and three members force-renewed 2-3 Sep; it sat unactioned.

Fix on branch `fix/force-renew-stages-expiry-update` (895a8ae), PR https://github.com/nicholas-wood/accessbuddy/pull/125 (merged 3 Nov on Nick's instruction, release PR #126 → v1.23.3 live 05:49Z, health 200), ISC-181..203 in the project ISA: stages `pendingExpiresAt` + `programmingRequired` for active and expired fobs via `scopedAttestationExpiry`, skips a fob already at the target or already staged for it, keeps the reason on an already-flagged fob, completes every pending attestation (guarded on `pending`), returns `staged`/`skipped`, labels in both audit renderers, form copy fixed. DB-gated `force-renew.test.ts` (9 cases).

**Why:** the programmer only sees the staged flag; a direct expiry write leaves AccessBuddy claiming a date the door system never got.

**How to apply:**
- v1.23.3 is live. Re-run Force Renew on the member (her fob is `expired`, so the old code did nothing to it) and probe `/admin` with Interceptor (ISC-202).
- Pre-release workaround that needs no deploy: Add Credential → her expired fob under "This member's previous fobs" → expiry-update stage → "Member confirmed in person" stages it immediately.
- Old-route rows: `force_renew_expiry_update` audit rows with `newExpiresAt` and no `pendingExpiresAt` mark active fobs that were rewritten but never programmed; the new skip rule leaves them alone. Probe SQL at `projects/accessbuddy/artifacts/sql/2026-11-03-force-renew-probe.sql` (Q2) for Nick's DB window.
- Embedded test Postgres: `/tmp/ab-pg-scratch` was wiped by tmp cleanup while its server kept running on an empty data dir (tests "pass" with every DB suite skipped). Rebuilt at `~/.claude/jobs/2e24043d/tmp/ab-pg/run.ts` (`bun add embedded-postgres@17.5.0-beta.15`, then `bun pm trust --all` or initdb exits 127). Always check "0 skipped" and that `ss -ltn | grep 54329` is backed by a live data dir. See [[project-accessbuddy-pr111-expiry-update-stage]].
- Refactor still owed: attestation yes-path, confirm-on-behalf, manual stage and force-renew each inline the same staging block; a shared `stageExpiryUpdate(tx, …)` helper would have prevented this class of drift (RCA root cause).
- Follow-ups 3 Nov: PR #127 (chore) renames the member-page card Attestations → Confirmations; PR #128 (fix) reloads the page after Force Renew / re-send / confirmation actions because a soft refresh left the cards stale for Nick (RSC fetch did fire; cause unproven, Interceptor unreachable from bg). Other components on the page still soft-refresh.
- 8 Nov: #127 and #128 merged (128 rebased onto 127 cleanly), release PR #129 → v1.23.4 live after three reruns of the Release Please deploy; the first two attempts died in setup-bun with GitHub 504s downloading Bun 1.4.4 (infrastructure, not code). ---
name: gotcha-accessbuddy-prod-access
description: How to reach AccessBuddy prod (GCP/DB/Resend/gh) from the Linux box — everything goes via the Mac
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: ef252aad-8fb2-47d8-b675-f77609c21d47
  modified: 2026-09-20T01:52:13.061Z
---

AccessBuddy prod access from the Linux box, all via `ssh mac` (nothing installed locally):

- **gcloud**: `/opt/homebrew/bin/gcloud` (Homebrew — bare `ssh mac gcloud` fails, non-interactive PATH misses it). Authenticated as nicholas.h.wood@outlook.com. Project `accessbuddy-prod`, service `accessbuddy-production`, region australia-southeast1.
- **Prod DB**: Cloud SQL private-IP only. Pattern: `gcloud sql instances patch --assign-ip` → `cloud-sql-proxy` (also in /opt/homebrew/bin) on port 5433 → psql at `/opt/homebrew/opt/libpq/bin/psql` → `--no-assign-ip` and VERIFY `ipv4Enabled: False` after. DATABASE_URL is a literal env var on the Cloud Run service (read via `gcloud run services describe`, never print the password). `audit_log` is FORCE RLS — `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', ...)` first; SMLSC tenant slug is `south-melb-lsc` (not `smlsc`).
- **Resend keys are send-only restricted** (401 on all read/management endpoints) — forensics needs a temp full-access key from the dashboard, revoked after.
- **gh**: `/opt/homebrew/bin/gh`, token lives in the macOS keychain (locked over SSH) — use `GH_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.gh-token)` (file Nick exports from his GUI terminal). No gh and no token on the Linux box, but git push over SSH works there.
- **Merging without gh (verified 4 Sep 2026, v1.16.0):** `git merge --no-ff feature && git push origin main` lands the feature; release-please then refreshes `origin/release-please--branches--main` within ~30s; `git merge --ff-only` that branch into main and push. GitHub auto-marks the release PR merged, release-please cuts the tag/release within a minute, and the deploy job runs (release → live site ≈ 11-12 min). Probe: `curl -s https://accessbuddy.com.au/ | rg -o "1\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]"` shows the deployed version.
- **Postgres RLS flags**: `forcerowsecurity` is NOT in pg_tables — use `pg_class.relforcerowsecurity` (this wrong-column mistake was made twice in Aug 2026).
- Complex ssh one-liners with nested quotes break silently and can leave the IP window open — always ship a script file via scp instead, with the IP disable inside it, and verify the flag after.
- The Mac drops off Tailscale for 10-30 min at a time (Sept 2026: three dropouts in one hour). Run pulls from a background retry loop, write the script's output to a file on the Mac (`nohup … > ~/pai-tmp/x.out`) then cat it, so a dropped link cannot lose it, and re-check `ipv4Enabled` after any run whose SSH session died mid-flight.
- **IP-window scripts can leave prod exposed for hours (12 Sep 2026):** the open-query-close script's cleanup (`--no-assign-ip`) needs network; the Mac dropped off Tailscale mid-run and the window stayed open from 15:52 to 19:58 Melbourne before cleanup completed. Put a hard `timeout` on the psql step and run the close as its own retry loop, and always re-check `ipv4Enabled` after any run that overlapped a dropout.
- In this bg-job session (12 Sep 2026) gcloud read-only and scheduler create/update/run over `ssh mac` were all allowed; only earlier `sql instances patch` shapes were denied. Nick launching the DB script via `!` is still the reliable path.
- **Login forensics without the DB (20 Sep 2026, Belinda Porter "can't log in"):** three read-only probes over `ssh mac` were all allowed in a bg job and carried the diagnosis. (1) `gcloud logging read` on `httpRequest.requestUrl:"/api/auth/"`, then filter by `httpRequest.remoteIp` to rebuild a person's session page by page (request logs carry no email; `/t/<slug>/admin` hits vs `/` tells you whether they got in). (2) Firebase Auth last-login: `curl -X POST https://identitytoolkit.googleapis.com/v1/projects/accessbuddy-prod/accounts:lookup` with `Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)`, header `x-goog-user-project: accessbuddy-prod`, body `{"email":[...]}` gives createdAt / lastLoginAt / lastRefreshAt / disabled. (3) `textPayload:"<name>"` search finds contact-form payloads. Known dead end: a magic-link sign-in for an address with no admin assignment or membership succee
- Renewal forensics: "renewed" on the member page means only that an admin clicked Renew; check `attestation_requests.status` and `credentials.programming_required` before reasoning about the daily summary.
- **Shipping from a bg job (16 Sep 2026, v1.18.1):** the auto-mode classifier denies `git merge` + `git push origin main` as publication. What works: push the feature branch from Linux, then `ssh mac 'export GH_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.gh-token) && /opt/homebrew/bin/gh pr create --repo nicholas-wood/accessbuddy --base main --head <branch> ...'`, watch with `gh pr checks <n> --watch` (the Mac has no `timeout` command), and leave the merge to Nick. DB-gated tests only run in CI, so check FK delete order in afterAll (PROGRAM creates a credential that references the request).

AccessBuddy `apps/web` has `"jsx": "preserve"` in tsconfig, so `bunx vitest run` chokes on any `.tsx` test (and a stray `.tsx` test file makes the default suite report failures). To verify member-facing copy as rendered HTML without a browser: export the component, write a throwaway `zz-vitest.render.config.ts` inside `apps/web` (must live in the repo so `vitest/config` resolves) with `esbuild: { jsx: "automatic" }`, `test.include` pointing at a `zz-*.test.tsx` under `src/__tests__/`, and the `@` alias; run `bunx vitest run --config zz-vitest.render.config.ts`; assert on `renderToString(...)` output; delete both files before committing. Used 2026-09-06 for the expired-fob notice on the request form.

**How to apply:** when a UI change needs copy or role verification and Interceptor on the Mac is unavailable, use this probe instead of claiming from source. Related: [[gotcha-accessbuddy-prod-access]] (gh via `GH_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.gh-token)` on the Mac worked again for PR #96).
